title: Aphelion navigation, curation folders, and heatmap deferral
content:
Aphelion had a practical pause-point pass focused on how the image wall is navigated, how curation folders resolve, and when a visualization idea should wait for better data.

What changed:

  • Keyboard navigation: the public grid now supports arrow-key movement through blocks, and Enter selects or clears the active block through the same path as a mouse click.
  • Nested curation folders: the admin catalog now sends real relative folder paths instead of display-style folder labels, so final subfolders under groups like 00 - Aphelion and 00 - AI should show their contained images correctly in the curation browser.
  • Weekly shuffle clarified: the current block refresh is automatic. Aphelion derives its grid order from the current ISO week seed and writes the matching weeklog file when that week first loads.
  • Heatmap deferred: we explored an isometric/3D-style map where x/y mirrored the weekly shuffled grid and z/height represented highlight count, then removed it from the live UI. The idea is worth revisiting later, but it will fit better once Aphelion has more highlight and download history.

The important decision was restraint. Keyboard browsing and correct folder filtering help the current workflow immediately; the heatmap should wait until there is enough real activity data for it to feel meaningful instead of decorative.
